Dativ Articles: Dem, Der, Den Exercises (A2)

Study four German examples with English meanings, then try four questions and check the explained answers.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the rule

Dativ often marks the receiver of something or follows prepositions like mit, nach and bei. Use dem (masculine/neuter), der (feminine), den (plural); plural nouns often add -n if possible.

Common mistake to avoid

Within the dative, den is the plural definite article; masculine singular takes dem. Outside the dative, den is also used for masculine accusative.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich helfe dem Mann.I help the man.
Worked example 2Sie spricht mit der Lehrerin.She speaks with the teacher.
Worked example 3Das gehört dem Kind.That belongs to the child.
Worked example 4Wir danken den Gästen.We thank the guests.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Use the dative definite article for each noun in brackets. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich fahre mit ___ Bus. (der Bus)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: dem

Mit always takes Dativ.

Question 2. Er hilft ___ Frau. (die Frau)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: der

Feminine Dativ takes der.

Question 3. Das Spielzeug gehört ___ Baby. (das Baby)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: dem

Neuter Dativ takes dem.

Question 4. Sie spricht mit ___ Kindern. (plural)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: den

Plural Dativ takes den, and Kindern has -n.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
